name: Volite / Volift

lead: Juvéderm Volite (also sold as Skinvive, gel VYC-12) is a crosslinked hyaluronic acid gel placed in the skin to give smoother, more hydrated, finer-textured skin, particularly on the cheeks, without adding volume. Volift is a different product in the same family, a filler for lines and folds.

The hyaluronic acid binds water in the dermis, which is meant to improve surface smoothness and hydration, and it is described as lower-concentration and longer-lasting than older boosters. Published work includes a prospective single-arm study in people with cheek roughness, a retrospective cohort, a small randomised split-face trial with botulinum toxin and several manufacturer-sponsored trials.

paras: A clinician injects small amounts of gel into the dermis at multiple points across the cheeks or other areas. It is often paired with botulinum toxin or fillers as a skin-quality step, with results assessed over the following weeks.

Reported effects are mainly injection-site swelling, redness and bruising. Hyaluronic acid fillers carry rarer risks including lumps, delayed inflammatory reactions and vascular complications. It is a regulated device administered by clinicians.

angle.text: Juvéderm Volite (VYC-12, also sold as Skinvive) is injected into the skin to leave it smoother and more hydrated rather than to add volume. The hyaluronic acid binds water in the dermis, improving surface texture. Trials exist, mostly single-arm and manufacturer-linked.

lead: Juvéderm Volite is a crosslinked hyaluronic acid (HA) gel (VYC-12, also marketed as Skinvive) injected intradermally to improve skin quality attributes such as surface smoothness and hydration.[1] It is described as providing longer-lasting effects at a lower HA concentration than traditional fillers.[2]

In a prospective single-arm study, patients with moderate or severe cheek skin roughness received VYC-12 in the cheeks and other areas, and the authors reported it as safe and effective for improving facial skin topography.[1] Other published work includes a Brazilian retrospective cohort,[2] a randomised split-face trial combined with botulinum toxin,[3] and several registered manufacturer-sponsored trials.[4][5][6]
Volift is a separate Juvéderm product name; the sources reviewed contain no clinical data on it specifically.
infobox: Single-arm, retrospective and one small randomised trial

paras: Hyaluronic acid fillers are generally crosslinked to prolong their duration.[7] Volite is positioned as a skin-quality product intended to improve texture and hydration instead of volume.[1][2]

A prospective single-arm study treated subjects with moderate or severe cheek skin roughness (on the Allergan Skin Roughness Scale) with VYC-12 and reported safety and effectiveness for skin topography.[1] A retrospective cohort of patients treated between 2018 and 2019 in Rio de Janeiro examined routine-practice use and safety.[2]
A randomised, double-blind split-face trial in 25 women combined onabotulinumtoxinA with Volite (Skinvive) for periorbital wrinkles and assessed efficacy and durability.[3]

Registered trials include a healthy-volunteer study of skin quality attributes,[8] studies in China for neck lines and perioral lines,[4][5] and a phase 2/3 skin quality study.[6] Their outcomes were not available in the sources reviewed.

Hyaluronic acid fillers can cause bruising, redness, pain, swelling, lumps, and rarely vascular occlusion or granulomatous reactions.[7] A 2026 computational study modelled risk of delayed immune and fibrotic reactions across 26 fillers and genotypes; it is a modelling analysis rather than a clinical trial.[9]
